record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.original_question: Does there exist a homogeneous subset of the real line R that is 1/2-CDH, meaning that it has exactly two equivalence classes of countable dense subsets under self-homeomorphisms?

evidence.quote: Problem 25. Is there a homogeneous 1 2 -CDH subset of R?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a separable topological space. Call two countable dense subsets D, E ⊆ X equivalent if there exists a homeomorphism h : X → X with h(D) = E; this is an equivalence relation on the family D(X) of all countable dense subsets of X. Let the CDH-number of X be the cardinality of D(X) modulo this relation. The space X is called n-CDH (for a cardinal n) if its CDH-number equals n; in particular, X is 1-CDH (i.e. countable dense homogeneous) if any two countable dense subsets are related by a self-homeomorphism, and X is (1/2)-CDH if it has exactly two equivalence classes of countable dense subsets. Recall that X is homogeneous if for every x, y ∈ X there is a homeomorphism of X carrying x to y.

Question: Does there exist a subset X ⊆ ℝ (with the subspace topology) such that X is homogeneous and X is (1/2)-CDH, i.e., the action of the self-homeomorphism group of X on its countable dense subsets has exactly two orbits?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface the original problem list and surrounding literature on countable dense homogeneity (works of Hrušák, van Mill, Medini and others), but no source located explicitly resolves the existence of a homogeneous (1/2)-CDH subset of ℝ. The status appears to still be open, but no definitive recent reference confirming resolution was found, so the status is recorded as unknown.
